Keeping the Fire of EDSA Alive
By Dr. Tony Leachon

The EDSA People Power Revolution was not just a political upheaval—it was a living testament to bayanihan, the Filipino spirit of unity. Without social media, smartphones, or email, millions of Filipinos found themselves shoulder to shoulder, guided only by faith, courage, and love for country.

June Keithley, the brave broadcaster, became the voice of EDSA. From Radio Veritas, she relayed vital information to the people, despite threats to her life. Her condition was one of immense personal risk—yet she chose to stand with the nation, amplifying the call for freedom.

Cardinal Jaime Sin, the moral compass of the time, played a pivotal role. His appeal to the faithful to protect Enrile and Ramos at Camp Aguinaldo and Camp Crame transformed a political standoff into a peaceful revolution. His voice carried the weight of conscience, reminding us that democracy is worth defending.

I was there, a postgraduate medical intern, among the two million Filipinos who filled EDSA. I witnessed ordinary citizens—priests, nuns, workers, students, families—become extraordinary in their courage. We prayed, we sang, we offered food and flowers to soldiers. We stood not for power, but for democracy.

Marcos Sr. was the most corrupt president in our history, and today, decades later, corruption has taken new forms under his son. The tragedy is that people power seems gone, replaced by division and political colors. Yet I believe hope remains. History teaches us that a tipping point will come.

For now, let us keep the fire burning. Let us continue to pray, to support our families and friends who have suffered through the years, and to remind ourselves that democracy is not a gift—it is a responsibility.

EDSA was proof that when Filipinos unite, miracles happen. And one day, when the nation is ready, we will rise again—not for one faction, but for the common good.

#RelentlessForChange

WILBEA FANS SPARK MASSIVE TREND AFTER SUCCESSFUL SHOW

The official tagline WILBEA PIÑASaya LOVESHOW ascended to the top of social media charts early this morning.

Dedicated supporters of Wilbert Ross and Bea Binene organized a massive digital rally to celebrate the pair’s latest appearance.

This surge in online activity follows their high-energy performance at Robinsons Las Piñas during a promotional event.

The duo, collectively known as WilBea, headlined the "Ganda Sa'yo Original Team" showcase to a jampacked crowd.

Thousands of fans, often called Wilbears or ka-oso, shared viral clips of the stars’ off-cam interactions and sweet gestures.

Digital footprints show the coordinated effort reached peak engagement levels throughout the Philippines and global entertainment circles.

Observers noted the intense protective behavior displayed by Ross toward Binene, fueling excitement among their loyal followers.

The event served as a high-profile promotion for their upcoming projects under the Viva Films production banner.

Despite limited television advertising, the grassroots fan-led movement secured the top trending spot across multiple platforms.

This phenomenon underscores the enduring power of celebrity pairings in the modern Philippine entertainment landscape.

#Unibearsity

🧾 PRESS RELEASE
SM Malls Average 115 Million Monthly Visits

ℹ️ Pasay City, Philippines [February 26, 2026] – SM Supermalls, the mall operations unit of SM Prime Holdings (SM Prime), averaged 115 million visits a month across its nationwide network in 2025.

Monthly foot traffic peaked at 153 million in December, typically the busiest period for retail centers. During the Christmas month, daily visits averaged 5.5 million on weekends and 4.6 million on weekdays.

Total mall visits reached 1.4 billion for the year, reflecting steady consumer activity despite challenging economic conditions and weather-related disruptions.
"As we marked our 40th anniversary last year, we reflected not only on what we have achieved, but on what the next four decades must become,” said SM Supermalls President Steven T. Tan. "With our customer as our North Star, we are evolving all for them, transforming their most-loved SM Supermalls not just to respond to needs, but to proactively anticipate them.”
Grounded in real-time customer insights, SM’s mall foot traffic was supported by innovative property attractions complemented by a dynamic tenant mix strategy, introducing first-in-market and first-in-SM experiences that continually refresh the mall journey.
On top of these, SM Supermalls launched a roadmap to deliver one flagship mall every year until 2030 alongside large-scale redevelopment initiatives across SM’s network of 89 malls.
In 2025, SM Supermalls opened MOA Sky and ScreenX, both the first of their kind in the Philippines. It also introduced SM Active Hub, the country’s largest and most inclusive sports playground.

These were complemented by the expansion of Book Nook reading spaces, purpose-led sustainability initiatives, and curated community events informed by customer sentiment.

During the period, SM Supermalls introduced several brands new to the Philippine market, including Chatterbox Café, Christy Ng, Funko, JD, Läderach, Mak’s Noodle, Oysho, Vivaia, and more.

Foot traffic is expected to remain resilient in 2026, supported by new destination concepts such as Southeast Asia’s first adidas Football Park and adidas Football Specialty Store, alongside the debut of Pop Mart’s first permanent Philippine store at SM Megamall. Both attractions were launched in late December.

“This year, we are bringing in new concepts that reflect how customers live, so every SM mall continues to feel personal, meaningful, and worth returning to,” added Tan.
###

🔗 Link: https://t.co/HFrpcZMuh0
